title: Honey and oat face mask
subtitle: A simple fresh mask for dry and sensitive skin
excerpt: A basic fresh face mask made with colloidal oat flour, raw honey, and plain yoghurt. The oat soothes, the honey humects, the yoghurt adds mild lactic acid for texture. Mixed to order and applied immediately. Makes two applications. No shelf life, use within 24 hours.
sourceNotes: Colloidal oatmeal (Avena sativa L.) in topical preparations: FDA recognised as an OTC skin protectant in 2003; approved for use in dry skin conditions. Active compounds include avenanthramides (anti-inflammatory), beta-glucan (occlusive/humectant). Raw honey: contains hydrogen peroxide and defensins (antimicrobial), naturally acidic (pH ~3.9), hygroscopic humectant. Yoghurt: lactic acid at low concentration provides very mild exfoliation; probiotic strains do not penetrate skin but may support the skin microbiome. Fresh mask only: water activity in yoghurt and honey supports microbial growth. Use within 24 hours, refrigerate if storing.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Mix to order. Any leftover mask can be refrigerated and used within 24 hours.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Use within 24 hours. The mask contains yoghurt and honey, both of which support microbial growth at room temperature once mixed. Refrigerate any remainder and discard after 24 hours.

glossaryTerms.definition: Oat flour ground fine enough to remain suspended in water rather than sinking. The fine particle size increases contact surface with the skin, delivering beta-glucan and avenanthramide compounds more effectively than whole oat flakes.
An ingredient that draws water from the air or deeper skin layers to the surface. Honey is a natural humectant, helping the skin feel softer and more hydrated during the mask.

content.text: Honey and oat face mask is a fresh, mix-to-order mask with three ingredients:
flour for its soothing and barrier-supporting compounds, raw honey as a natural
, and plain whole-milk yoghurt for mild lactic acid and a smooth texture. Applied for 10-15 minutes then rinsed off. Makes two applications.

items.prepNote: approx. 2 tbsp; or rolled oats blitzed to fine powder in a blender
approx. 1 tbsp; natural humectant and antimicrobial
approx. 1 tbsp; whole milk; adds mild lactic acid for texture

content.text: Mix all three ingredients together in a small bowl until smooth. The mixture should be thick and spreadable, if too stiff, add a little more yoghurt a teaspoon at a time.
Apply to clean, dry face, avoiding the eye area. Spread in an even layer.
Leave for 10-15 minutes. Rinse with warm water and pat dry.

Test on the inner arm before applying to the face, particularly if you have a known sensitivity to oats, honey, or dairy. Oat protein can cause contact dermatitis in some people with coeliac disease or wheat allergy.
Use within 24 hours. Refrigerate any leftover mask. Discard if it smells sour or shows any visible spoilage.
